clue.text: Young man much admired a bird with nothing on

parts.note: a poll is a parrot, the traditional pet bird of crosswords
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An admired youth, apparently a naked bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing on' sets O after A and POLL rather than meaning undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the sun god was the ideal of male beauty, so his name is used for any strikingly handsome youth.

clue.text: Individual characters make an impression

definitions.meaning: writing letters separately rather than in joined-up script

explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting in separate capitals has this name, and pressing ink onto paper with type is the press's job.

clue.text: On the other side in the French game

indicators.note: in means the phrase for the other side goes inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
across means over on the far side

explanation.surface: Something on the far side of a French game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'the French' gives the French article rather than describing the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Spring one trap, and talk at length about it

indicators.note: about means the speech word goes around the others

parts.note: to orate is to give a long speech
I is the Roman numeral one
a gin is a snare for catching animals

explanation.surface: Set off a snare, then talk at length about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring one trap' reads as triggering a snare, but 'Spring' is the definition, meaning arise; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from something is to arise or start from it, to have its source there.

clue.text: It'll provide assistance if flier's arranged to come in

definitions.text: It'll provide assistance if flier's arranged to come in

indicators.note: to come in means these letters go inside the word for help

parts.note: aid means assistance or help

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the airman word are put in a new order

parts.note: a flier is a pilot or airman; the 's is not a letter

explanation.surface: Something helps a pilot to land once things are arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' is the anagram signal and 'to come in' the container signal; the whole clue also describes the answer, a place that helps pilots land.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing ground is the place that helps a pilot land, which is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Refuse collector shifted deal of old litter

indicators.note: shifted means these letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A binman moved a quantity of old rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The refuse collector is the dustman father of Eliza in Shaw's play Pygmalion (and My Fair Lady).
explanation.definitionFit: In Shaw's Pygmalion Eliza's father is a dustman, a man paid to collect household rubbish.

clue.text: Some foliage used by gardener, initially, for dressing

definitions.text: Some foliage used by gardener, initially, for dressing

parts.words: Some foliage used by gardener, initially, for dressing
parts.note: the first gardener is Adam in Eden, who covered himself with a leaf from a fruit tree at the beginning of time

explanation.walkthrough: 'gardener, initially' means the first gardener, Adam, not a gardener's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve sewed these leaves into coverings in Genesis, hence a token covering.

clue.text: Monarch's contributed to tax, in practice

indicators.note: contributed to means the monarch's letters are put into the tax word

parts.note: excise is a duty charged on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen; the 's means 'has'

explanation.surface: The sovereign has paid tax, in practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributed to' is the container signal; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's usual monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise means drill or practice, as in a training exercise.

clue.text: I had set up firm in this region

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the short form is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
strict means firm or stern

explanation.surface: Someone founded a business in this area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' looks like founding a firm; it reverses ID to DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area or locality.

clue.text: Motorway's main cause of injury

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway (as in Britain's M1), and the 's is read as 'is'
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A motorway is said to be the leading cause of road injuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief in its older sense is harm or damage, the thing that hurts someone.

clue.text: Return material to front of shop — that's a way out

indicators.note: Return tells us to read the fabric word from right to left

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woven fabric, a material

indicators.note: front of means only the opening letter of shop is used

explanation.surface: Taking cloth back to a store is the way to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' is the reversal signal and 'front of' takes the first letter of 'shop'; serge is a twilled worsted cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit, a door or passage for leaving.

clue.text: Deadly stuff heartless poisoner ordered at first?

indicators.note: first says the word at comes at the front of the answer
ordered means the remaining letters are put into a new sequence
heartless means the two central letters of poisoner are removed

explanation.surface: A heartless poisoner wonders whether some lethal substance was what they ordered first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the two middle letters, 'ordered' is the anagram signal, and 'at first' puts the little word in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a poisonous alkaloid from deadly nightshade, a lethal substance.

clue.text: Sportsman takes barrier on course right

parts.note: a fence is a jump on a racecourse or showjumping course

explanation.surface: A rider takes a jump on the course correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a horse race; the sportsman is a swordsman instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer is an athlete who competes with foil, épée or sabre.

clue.text: Rugby player to keep well away from

definitions.meaning: in rugby union the fly-half is also called by this name, the back who stands off from the scrum
to hold back at a distance, remaining aloof

explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the fly-half position has this name, and as a verb phrase it means remaining apart or aloof.

clue.text: Weapon used to make pirate secure

parts.note: Captain Flint is the pirate in Treasure Island
to lock is to make secure

explanation.surface: A gun used to keep a buccaneer safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Flint is the dead pirate captain of Stevenson's Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A flintlock is an old firearm whose charge is lit by a spark from flint.

clue.text: Turn round and leer without hesitation?

definitions.text: Turn round and leer without hesitation?

indicators.note: round tells us to turn the word for a turn back to front

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: without means the letters for hesitation are taken out of leer

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone spins about and leers openly, without a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses the word for a turn and 'without' drops the hesitation sound; the whole clue also describes the act.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare lustfully at someone is to give them a lecherous look.

clue.text: University pair forming neat link

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a bridge is a link between two places

explanation.surface: Two universities form a tidy connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' reads as tidy but is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The term combines the names of Oxford and Cambridge, England's two oldest universities.

clue.text: Some securities newly issued could be a risky venture

parts.note: longs are long-dated government stocks
hot means fresh, as in hot off the press

explanation.surface: New shares might be a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: LONGS are British gilts with long maturities.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is an attempt or bet with little chance of success.

clue.text: Pronounced poetic pieces a great achievement

indicators.note: Pronounced signals a word that is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: feet are the metrical units of a line of poetry

explanation.surface: Reciting verse well is said to be a great accomplishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a remarkable deed or exploit.

clue.text: Agricultural worker's strong body parts

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud or strong
the arm is a body part
the hand is another body part

explanation.surface: A labourer on the land has a powerful physique.
explanation.walkthrough: F (forte) is the musical sign for strong or loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhand is a labourer employed on a farm.

clue.text: He is involved with the ultimate in exquisite taste

definitions.text: He is involved with the ultimate in exquisite taste

indicators.note: is involved with means the letters are tangled together into a new order
the ultimate in means only the last letter of exquisite is taken

explanation.surface: A man engaged with the very finest taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved with' mixes HE, E (last of 'exquisite') and TASTE; the clue as a whole describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person with refined sensitivity to beauty and art.

clue.text: Foreign girl runs into trouble in Estonia

indicators.note: into means the letter for runs is inserted in the jumbled letters
trouble in means the letters of Estonia are stirred up

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A young foreign woman gets into difficulties in the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble in' scrambles ESTONIA and 'into' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Way a bird collected vital bits of flowers

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the mina, or mynah, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: A roadside bird gathered pollen-bearing parts of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses an old plural of stamen, the pollen-bearing organ; 'collected' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: In old botanical usage this is a plural of stamen, the male fertile organ of a bloom.

clue.text: Pop music in key obscured by enthusiastic backing

indicators.note: obscured by means the key letter is hidden inside the other word
backing means the word for enthusiastic is written in reverse

parts.note: eager means keen or enthusiastic
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A pop song in a certain key is drowned out by keen backing singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns EAGER into REGAE and 'obscured by' hides G in it; 'backing' poses as backing vocals.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggae is a style of popular music from Jamaica.

clue.text: It's held back by resident for a buddy

indicators.note: held means one word is gripped inside the other

parts.note: an inmate is a resident of an institution

indicators.note: back means the little word is read in reverse

parts.note: the word it, with the 's acting as 'is'

explanation.surface: Something is kept back by a lodger for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the little word and 'held' is the container signal; 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate is a close friend or confidant.

clue.text: Hard-hearted artist takes a flower

indicators.note: hearted means the letter for hard goes into the middle of the painter's name

parts.note: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An unfeeling painter picks a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-hearted' looks like callous; it puts H in the heart of DALI, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden plant with showy blooms, named after a Swedish botanist.

clue.text: Untrustworthy as, for example, sovereign is

definitions.meaning: deceitful, saying one thing and doing another
a sovereign is a British gold coin, which like any coin has a head and a tail side

explanation.definitionFit: A hypocrite shows two faces, and a coin has literally two faces, obverse and reverse.

clue.text: Drive off as convertible gets near

indicators.note: convertible means the letters can be changed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Driving away in an open-top car as it gets close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive off' and 'convertible' together suggest motoring; 'convertible' scrambles GETS NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to push them away emotionally.

clue.text: Sort of organ

definitions.meaning: kind or type, as in the phrase 'of that ...'
one of the pair of organs that filter the blood

explanation.definitionFit: The word means temperament or kind in old usage, and is also the name of a blood-filtering bodily organ.
